thread:
incident-bot: PAGE -> P1: runtime.runtime_service: multiple GPU OOMs observed on prod-gpu-pool (model-x). Start 2026-03-15T02:12:00Z. Symptoms: 5xx rate spike, increased tail latency, some requests retrying. Paging oncall.

sara: I'm oncall, grabbing it. @omar can you pull NVML + runtime heap stats? I'll open a quick customer note draft and ping CS.

omar: looking. Initial grep of runtime logs shows repeated "alloc failed" in allocator and frequent 'kv_cache_page_fault' traces. Pulling nvidia-smi & dmesg now.

omar: paste: ```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv
index, memory.total [MiB], memory.used [MiB]
0, 49152 MiB, 47210 MiB
1, 49152 MiB, 46890 MiB
2, 49152 MiB, 49010 MiB
```

omar: also runtime logs snippet: ```
2026-03-15T02:11:58Z runtime: alloc failed: 8192 bytes, used=49010 MiB, free_contig=120 MiB
2026-03-15T02:12:01Z runtime: kv_cache_page_fault: shard=3 entries=124k, pagewalks=230
2026-03-15T02:12:05Z runtime: OOM evict failed
```

liz: thx. That looks like fragmentation/contiguous-free issue, not just overall usage. We saw similar on a long-tail workload where large sequence lengths caused the allocator to fail to find contiguous blocks.

derek: can we reduce batch_size or max_seq for model-x as a quick mitigation? We could also temporarily disable prefix KV caching for the busiest routes to avoid large KV growth.

sara: do it. @derek reduce global batch_size for model-x to 1 and set kv_cache.enabled=false for model-x route. Anyone foresee customer breakage from that? @cs-rep please advise.

cs-rep: FYI: two customers reported increased retries but no data loss. They're okay with temporary perf hits if it stabilizes.

deploy-bot: deploy queued by derek: change model-x batch_size=1, kv_cache.enabled=false -> staging -> canary -> prod (auto-promote).

omar: implementing mitigation: temporarily scaled instance group to add two spare GPUs for headroom and amped eviction aggressiveness (kv_cache.eviction_threshold -> 0.6). Pushing config now.

omar: After mitigation (02:15 UTC) quick metrics: 5xx count down 70% in 3m. Still seeing one GPU with fragmentation warnings in dmesg.

liz: good. Need NVML heap dump from that GPU (index 2 earlier). Can someone run: ```sudo ./nvml-dump --gpu 2 > /tmp/gpu2-dump.log``` and upload to s3.

omar: uploaded: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1948765555/gpu2-dump.log

sara: building timeline here (rough):
- 02:11:58 alert: allocator reported contiguous-free low
- 02:12:00 pager triggered
- 02:13:00 oncall engaged
- 02:15:00 mitigation applied (batch_size->1, kv_cache disabled for route)
- 02:18:30 observable drop in 5xxs
- 02:22:00 continued low-level pagewalk alerts on single node

derek: hypothesis list:
1) KV cache growth -> fragmented GPU address space -> contiguous allocation failures for large attention buffers
2) Long-lived processes pinning allocations (no defrag path) causing slowly increasing fragmentation
3) Kernel-level pagewalk/backing-store thrash under heavy concurrent allocation

liz: initial signal favors (1) + (2). We see high pagewalk counts and large kv_cache shard sizes. We should collect per-shard entry sizes and sequence-length distribution. Omar, can you attach a sample of kv cache stats: ```curl -s http://localhost:9300/metrics/kvcache | jq .shards``` and upload.

omar: pasted snapshot: ```
{ "shard_3": { "entries": 124000, "avg_entry_size": 512, "hot_fraction": 0.9 },
  "shard_7": { "entries": 98k, "avg_entry_size": 480 }
}
```

liz: average entry ~500 bytes but hot_fraction 0.9 means many entries are in-use and pinned. Eviction threshold tweak should help but we may need an adaptive eviction or size cap per-route.

sara: for the RCA thread I'll need concrete artifacts: nvml dumps, runtime logs (02:10-02:30), kvcache snapshots, and the canary deploy diff. Omar/Derek please link them here.

omar: runtime logs uploaded: s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1948765555/runtime-02-10-02-30.log

derek: canary diff: git rev 9a3b2 -> 9a3b3 (batch_size change + kv flag toggle) deployed at 02:15. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/deploys/9a3b3

liz: quick experiment idea for post-incident: run a controlled repro with synthetic long sequences and high prefix cache to see fragmentation pattern, then test an allocator tweak (coalesce free ranges every N allocations). If that repros we can design a scheduler that rotates workloads before fragmentation reaches critical.

sara: agreed. For customer comms I'm drafting a short note: "We saw transient OOMs caused by KV cache driven fragmentation. We applied mitigations (reduced batch size and disabled route-level cache) and added temporary capacity. We're investigating persistent fix options and will follow up." Any edits?

cs-rep: fine. Add apology and ETA for RCA doc by EOD PST.

omar: quick additional datapoint: GPU 2 had three processes holding pinned buffers from previous model versions (older sessions). Killing the older agent processes reduced fragmentation immediately on that node. I suspect stale pinned allocations + high kv cache entries amplified it.

derek: action items (assigned):
- derek: implement auto-disable of kv_cache when shard entries > 100k for a route (short-term config) [IN-PROGRESS]
- omar: collect repro harness + nvml dump analysis [IN-PROGRESS]
- liz: design allocator coalescing / defrag proposal [PENDING]
- sara: customer comms + incident doc [IN-PROGRESS]

sara: handoff: I'll be on for 15 more minutes, then handing to @liz (next-day oncall) with summary + artifacts. @liz please confirm you have write access to s3 bucket and the deploy links.

liz: confirmed, I have access. I'll continue timeline + start the controlled repro tomorrow morning my timezone. Adding more detailed notes to the RCA doc at s3://redwood-incident-docs/1948765555/rca.md

sara: final note: watch for reoccurrence over next 6 hours; if we see >2 similar OOMs escalate back to P0. Marking this thread as incident->mitigated and moving to RCA prep. :white_check_mark:
